## Summary

This PR fixes proxy support for AWS Bedrock nodes by updating to `@langchain`/aws v0.1.14 and utilizing the newly introduced clientOptions API for proxy configuration.

AWS Bedrock nodes (LmChatAwsBedrock and EmbeddingsAwsBedrock) were not respecting proxy settings configured in n8n. Earlier versions of `@langchain`/aws (v0.1.13 and below) did not provide a clean way to configure proxy settings, and the existing implementation used undici's ProxyAgent which is incompatible with AWS SDK's underlying HTTP client.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent the app from crashing or returning to Home when Gemini returns 404/429 or when the response body is missing or malformed. 
- Make JSON parsing and role detection defensive to avoid NPEs and brittle assumptions.

### Description
- Hardened `ChatActivity` response handling by null-checking `response.body()`, returning early on non-2xx responses, and showing user-friendly messages via `addMessage(...)` instead of allowing brittle parsing to throw. 
- Added `extractAiText(String)` that uses `opt*` JSON accessors to safely extract `candidates -> content -> parts -> text`, and added `buildApiErrorMessage(int,String)` that maps `429` and `404` to clear guidance. 
- Tidied imports and minor fixes: removed an unused `Handler` import and wired an API key constant used by the activity. 
- Fixed adapter/model role handling and UI binding: added `TextView` import in `ChatAdapter`, changed `getItemViewType` to use `"user".equals(getSentBy())`, and added `SENT_BY_USER` constant plus `isUser()` helper to `ChatMessage` for null-safe role checks.

### Testing
- Ran a code search for the new helpers and branches with `rg "buildApiErrorMessage|extractAiText|response\.body\(\) != null|statusCode == 429|statusCode == 404"` which confirmed the new logic was present and referenced. ✅
- Attempted to run unit tests with `bash ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --no-daemon`, but Gradle distribution download is blocked by the environment proxy (HTTP 403), so unit tests could not be executed. ⚠️

body:
### Motivation
- Align the dashboard UI with recently extended detector output that adds FRED plumbing/funding signals and explicit freshness metadata. 
- Increase robustness of the detector against missing/NaN tails from rolling windows and mixed calendar stamps. 
- Replace the old share-volume proxy with a SPY dollar-volume z-score for a more stable liquidity signal. 
- Provide a freshness guardrail so runs with stale inputs surface as `data_stale` rather than producing misleading alerts or crashes. 

### Description
- In `scripts/dislocation_detector.py`: add `DEFAULT_FRED_SERIES` and accept a `fred_map` to auto-fetch multiple FRED series; implement `safe_last` (returns `Optional[float]`) and `safe_bool` helpers, add `bday_lag_days` to compute business-day lags, and introduce `RunMeta` to carry `equity_session_date`, stale info and related metadata. 
- Harden `compute_signals` by aligning on the equity session index as the master, switching to SPY dollar-volume z-score (`spy_dollar_vol_z`), cleaning/reindexing/ffilling VIX (drop non-positive levels, ignore extreme 1d jumps unless equities corroborate, reindex/ffill), and adding new FRED-backed signals: `credit_spread_widening_fred`, `funding_stress_sofr_iorb`, `repo_rate_volume_dislocation`, and `rates_volatility_shock`. 
- Change counting logic to exclude `forced_flow_proxy_combo` from the K-count so it remains explanatory, and update `derive_status` to return `data_stale` when inputs are stale. 
- Extend `summarize_dislocation` output to include `data_dates` with `equity_session_date`, `vix_stale_days`, `data_stale`, and `stale_reasons`. 
- UI updates in `dislocation/index.html` and `public/dislocation/index.html`: add new pretty names and hints for the FRED/funding signals, switch liquidity hint to `spy_dollar_volume_z`, add handling for `data_stale` (badge/headline/explanation), and render `equity_session_date` + explicit `stale_reasons`; sync `public/` copy with source. 

### Testing
- Served the site locally with `python -m http.server 4173 --directory .` and verified the updated page rendered without errors. (Succeeded.)

author: anfredette
body:
## Summary

- Restructure backend modules to match the 5-component architecture
  defined in ARCHITECTUREv2.md: Intent Extraction, Specification,
  Recommendation, Configuration, and Infrastructure (cluster/API)
- Split monolithic `context_intent/` into `intent_extraction/`,
  `specification/`, and `shared/schemas/`
- Split `deployment/` into `configuration/` (YAML generation) and
  `cluster/` (K8s management)
- Split 1190-line `api/routes.py` into 6 modular route files with
  shared dependency injection
- Rename recommendation internals to match architecture terminology
  (ConfigFinder, Scorer, Analyzer)
- Add service facade classes for each component
- Standardize all API endpoints under `/api/v1/` prefix, replacing
  inconsistent mix of full paths and missing prefixes across route files

## Details

No functional or behavioral changes. All existing API endpoints,
business logic, and data flows are preserved. This is a pure
structural refactoring to improve maintainability and align the
codebase with the documented architecture.

### Module mapping (old → new)

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `context_intent/extractor.py` | `intent_extraction/extractor.py` |
| `context_intent/traffic_profile.py` | `specification/traffic_profile.py` |
| `context_intent/schema.py` | `shared/schemas/` (split into intent, specification, recommendation) |
| `context_intent/gpu_normalizer.py` | `shared/utils/gpu_normalizer.py` |
| `deployment/generator.py`, `validator.py`, `templates/` | `configuration/` |
| `deployment/cluster.py` | `cluster/manager.py` |
| `api/routes.py` | `api/app.py` + `api/dependencies.py` + `api/routes/*.py` |
| `recommendation/capacity_planner.py` | `recommendation/config_finder.py` |
| `recommendation/solution_scorer.py` | `recommendation/scorer.py` |
| `recommendation/ranking_service.py` | `recommendation/analyzer.py` |
| `recommendation/usecase_quality_scorer.py` | `recommendation/quality/usecase_scorer.py` |

### API path standardization

All route files now use `APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1")` with relative
paths in decorators. Previously, `recommendation.py` and
`configuration.py` used full paths without a prefix (e.g.,
`@router.post("/api/deploy")`), while other route files already used
the prefix pattern. This was inconsistent but not a backward
compatibility concern since the project is pre-release.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `/api/recommend` | `/api/v1/recommend` |
| `/api/ranked-recommend-from-spec` | `/api/v1/ranked-recommend-from-spec` |
| `/api/deploy` | `/api/v1/deploy` |
| `/api/deploy-to-cluster` | `/api/v1/deploy-to-cluster` |
| `/api/cluster-status` | `/api/v1/cluster-status` |
| `/api/deployments/...` | `/api/v1/deployments/...` |
| `/health` | `/health` (unchanged) |

Updated all references in `ui/app.py`, `tests/test_kubernetes_deployment.py`,
`ui/TESTING.md`, and documentation files. Added API endpoint conventions
to `CLAUDE.md` to enforce consistency going forward. Fixed stale file
path references in `CLAUDE.md` from the module restructuring.

## Test plan

- [ ] Backend starts successfully (`make run-backend`)
- [ ] Full workflow works end-to-end (chat → spec → recommendations → YAML generation)
- [ ] All API endpoints are under `/api/v1/` (verify via `/docs` or route listing)
- [ ] `/health` remains at root (no prefix)
- [ ] UI connects to updated endpoint paths without errors

author: sannidhyaroy
body:
## Summary
This pull request migrates the application's logging system from `CleanroomLogger` to Apple's Unified Logging (`os.Logger`) API. It removes all dependencies and references to the unmaintained `CleanroomLogger` library, updates the codebase to use the new logging API, improves log categorization for easier filtering, and revises the documentation and acknowledgements to reflect these changes. Additionally, it improves log privacy handling and provides updated instructions for debugging and viewing logs.

---

### Logging System Migration
- Introduced a new `Logger+Categories.swift` file defining custom Logger categories (`general`, `filesystem`, `sharing`, `ui`, `network`, `config`) for structured logging throughout the app, replacing the previous CleanroomLogger setup.
- Removed all CleanroomLogger imports and configuration code, and replaced all `Log.*?.message` calls with the appropriate `Logger.*` calls, including privacy annotations for log data.
- Removed the `CleanroomLogger` dependency from `Cartfile`, effectively dropping `CleanroomLogger` entirely from our project.

---

### Project Configuration Updates
- Removed `CleanroomLogger` framework from the Xcode Project and added the new `Logger+Categories.swift` source file to the project and build phases.

---

### Documentation and Debugging Updates
- Updated the `README.md` to explain the new logging system, including how to view and persist logs using `log` commands and Console.app, and removed instructions related to `CleanroomLogger`. Added privacy and security warnings for debug logging.
- Removed references of `CleanroomLogger` from `Acknowledgments.html`.

These changes ensure all logging is now handled by the native `os.Logger` API, providing better integration with system tools and more maintainable, categorized log output.

hieblmi
body:
_partially addresses https://github.com/lightninglabs/aperture/issues/192_

Aperture supports an alternative authentication method based on proof-of-work
(PoW) instead of Lightning payments. This allows services to gate access behind
a computational cost rather than a monetary one, which is useful for rate
limiting, spam prevention, or environments where Lightning infrastructure is
unavailable.

PoW authentication is configured per service. A single Aperture instance can
serve both Lightning-authenticated and PoW-authenticated services
simultaneously.

Protocol Flow:
```
Client                                    Aperture                        Backend
  |                                          |                               |
  |  1. GET /api/resource                    |                               |
  |----------------------------------------->|                               |
  |                                          |                               |
  |  2. 402 Payment Required                 |                               |
  |     WWW-Authenticate: L402               |                               |
  |       macaroon="<base64>",               |                               |
  |       pow="<difficulty>"                 |                               |
  |<-----------------------------------------|                               |
  |                                          |                               |
  |  3. Client solves PoW:                   |                               |
  |     SHA256(tokenID || nonce) has         |                               |
  |     <difficulty> leading zero bits       |                               |
  |                                          |                               |
  |  4. Client adds pow caveat to macaroon   |                               |
  |     and retries:                         |                               |
  |     Authorization: L402 <mac>:POW        |                               |
  |----------------------------------------->|                               |
  |                                          |  5. Forward authenticated     |
  |                                          |     request                   |
  |                                          |------------------------------->|
  |                                          |                               |
  |                                          |  6. Response                   |
  |                                          |<-------------------------------|
  |  7. Response                             |                               |
  |<-----------------------------------------|                               |
```

author: nickfalcone
body:
The alert summary hash (used as both the React Query key and the server-side KV cache key) only included id + severity. Since the summarization prompt now uses updatedAt for conflict resolution and title/summary for content, changes to these fields could serve a stale cached summary. Include all summarization-relevant fields in the hash input so caches invalidate when content or recency changes.

 Problem: computeAlertsHash only used id + severity in its hash   
  input, but the summarization prompt depends on updatedAt (for
  conflict resolution) and title/summary (for content). This meant 
  both the client-side React Query cache key and the server-side KV
   cache key (summary:${hash}) could serve stale summaries when
  those fields changed without an id/severity change.

  Fix in src/utils/alertSummaryApi.ts: Updated the hash input from
  ${id}:${severity} to
  ${id}:${severity}:${title}:${summary}:${updatedAt} so the hash
  changes whenever any summarization-relevant field changes.

  Tests in src/utils/alertSummaryApi.test.ts: Added three new test
  cases verifying the hash changes when updatedAt, title, or
  summary change independently.

Follow-up from https://github.com/nickFalcone/charlotte-watch/pull/35

The site had no OpenGraph or Twitter Card metadata, resulting in poor/missing social media previews when links are shared.

## Changes

**Root Layout** (`src/app/layout.tsx`)
- Added base metadata: `metadataBase`, OpenGraph properties (type, locale, url, siteName, images), Twitter Card properties
- Type annotated with `Metadata` from Next.js
- Uses existing `android-chrome-512x512.png` as default social preview image

**Homepage** (`src/app/page.tsx`)
- Added page-specific metadata with images (inherits and overrides layout metadata)

**Blog Posts** (`src/app/posts/[slug]/page.tsx`)
- Implemented `generateMetadata()` for dynamic, per-post metadata
- Fetches title, description, publishDate from database
- Sets OpenGraph type to "article" with author and publish date

## Implementation Notes

All image URLs use absolute paths (`https://ncrmro.com/...`) for compatibility with social media crawlers. Page-level metadata completely replaces (not merges) layout metadata for the same property, so images must be explicitly included in both layout and page-level `openGraph` objects.

```typescript
export const metadata: Metadata = {
  metadataBase: new URL("https://ncrmro.com"),
  openGraph: {
    images: [{
      url: "https://ncrmro.com/android-chrome-512x512.png",
      width: 512,
      height: 512,
    }],
  },
  twitter: {
    card: "summary",
    images: ["https://ncrmro.com/android-chrome-512x512.png"],
  },
};
```

Generates proper `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:image`, `og:type`, `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image` tags for all pages.

This PR addresses identified vulnerabilities in the repository.

1.  **Vulnerable Dependencies**: `requirements.txt` has been updated to pin secure versions of `Pillow`, `requests`, and `jinja2`.
2.  **DoS Vulnerability**: The `_handle` function in `ai1.py` previously read the entire uploaded file into memory to calculate its hash. This has been refactored to read the file in 8KB chunks, preventing potential Memory Exhaustion DoS attacks.
3.  **Tests**: The unit tests in `tests/test_fix.py` have been updated to support and verify the chunked reading implementation using `mock_file.read.side_effect`.

author: lailoo
body:
## Summary

Fixes #10332 — Compaction truncates history even when summary generation fails, leaving only the useless fallback text "Summary unavailable due to context limits."

## Root Cause

In `compaction-safeguard.ts`, three failure paths (no model, no API key, summarization exception) all returned a compaction result with `firstKeptEntryId`, which told the framework to proceed with truncation despite having no meaningful summary. This caused catastrophic context loss ("amnesia").

## Fix

Return `{ cancel: true }` in all three failure paths instead of a fallback compaction result. The pi-coding-agent framework already supports `cancel` in `SessionBeforeCompactResult` — when set, it throws `"Compaction cancelled"` and preserves the full session history.

### Changed paths:
- **No model** → `{ cancel: true }` + warning log
- **No API key** → `{ cancel: true }` + warning log
- **Summarization throws** → `{ cancel: true }` + warning log (was: "truncating history")

## Tests

### Unit tests (3 regression tests)
1. Cancels compaction when model is unavailable
2. Cancels compaction when API key is unavailable
3. Cancels compaction when summarization throws (via `vi.spyOn` mock)

### Live test (LIVE=1)
- Added a live integration test in `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` that calls a real LLM to verify compaction produces a meaningful summary (not cancel) when model + API key are available.
- Skipped automatically when `LIVE=1` is not set or API key is missing.
- Verified with `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` via custom Anthropic endpoint.

### Standalone script
- `scripts/test-compaction-live.ts` — standalone verification script that tests both `summarizeInStages` and the full extension handler with a real LLM.

All 5032 tests pass (5031 unit + 1 live).

## Files Changed
- `src/agents/pi-extensions/compaction-safeguard.ts` — 3 failure paths now return `{ cancel: true }`
- `src/agents/pi-extensions/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` — 3 regression tests + 1 live test
- `scripts/test-compaction-live.ts` — standalone live verification script
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry added

author: copilot
body:
## Description

TypeScript compilation failed due to `JobStatus` and `WorkloadCategory` types being unavailable in `src/features/hpc/types/index.ts` at lines 95 and 117.

### Changes

- **lib/portal/index.ts**: Exported all missing HPC types (`WorkloadCategory`, `JobResources`, `JobParameter`, `JobSubmissionState`, `JobSubmissionStep`, `JobPriceQuote`, `JobValidationError`, `JobStatusChange`, `JobEventType`, `JobOutputType`, `HPCError`, `HPCErrorCode`)
- **portal/src/lib/portal-adapter.ts**: Re-exported all HPC types to maintain consistent import paths
- **portal/src/features/hpc/types/index.ts**: Added separate `import type` statement before `export type` to make types available for local use within the file

The issue occurred because TypeScript `export type` re-exports types without making them available in the same module's scope. Types must be explicitly imported to be used locally:

```typescript
// Import for local use
import type { JobStatus, WorkloadCategory } from '@/lib/portal-adapter';

// Re-export for consumers
export type { JobStatus, WorkloadCategory } from '@/lib/portal-adapter';

// Now these can be used in local interfaces
export interface JobFilters {
  status?: JobStatus[];  // ✓ Now resolves correctly
}
```

body:
## Summary

Add `json_append_object` function that builds a JSON object from key=value arguments and appends it to an array. All values are stored as strings, consistent with the existing `json_set` pattern.

Closes #4

## File Context (for reviewers)

### Files changed

**`bash-json-file.sh`**
- Module-level constants used in diff:
  - `_JSON_ERR_JQ=2` (L27) — exit code for jq/argument errors
- Internal helpers called in diff but defined elsewhere:
  - `_json_error()` (L36) — stderr error output
  - `_json_modify()` (L123) — core read-modify-write with jq
- Public API the new function follows patterns from:
  - `json_append()` (L339) — existing array append (raw JSON)
  - `json_set()` (L316) — existing string value setter (--arg pattern)
- CLI dispatch: `_json_main()` (L376) — case statement for command routing
- Usage text: `_json_usage()` (L352) — help output

**`test/test_append_object.sh`**
- New file: 16 tests / 19 assertions
- Uses test framework from `test/test_helper.sh` and `test/test_framework.sh`

**`README.md`**
- API table: added `json_append_object` row
- Type handling section: added note about string-only values

## Goal / Non-Goals

**Goal:**
- Simplify string-only object append from 2 lines (`jq -nc` + `json_append`) to 1 line
- Keep `jq -nc` usage internal to the library
- Maintain consistency with `json_set` (string) / `json_set_raw` (raw JSON) pattern

**Non-Goals:**
- `json_append_object_raw` variant for mixed types (use existing `json_append` + `jq -nc`)
- Nested object support in key=value syntax
- Key deduplication or ordering guarantees

## Existing Safety Mechanisms

- **`_json_modify` output validation**: Validates jq produces exactly one JSON value (L144-149)
- **Atomic writes**: `mktemp` + `mv` in `_json_write_atomic` prevents partial writes
- **`--` separator**: All jq invocations use `--` to prevent filename option injection

## Code Patterns

- String values use `jq --arg` binding (never interpolated into filter)
- Key names also use `--arg` binding to prevent jq filter injection
- Error messages do not expose raw input values
- Exit code 2 for argument validation errors (consistent with CLI dispatch pattern)

## Accepted Risks

- **Key ordering in constructed objects**: jq determines key order; no guarantee of insertion order.
  - Reason: JSON spec does not require key ordering
  - Fallback: Use `json_append` + hand-crafted JSON for order-sensitive cases

## Test Plan

- [x] Single key=value pair appends correctly
- [x] Multiple key=value pairs construct proper object
- [x] Nested array path works
- [x] Multiple sequential appends
- [x] Values with spaces, special characters, equals signs
- [x] Empty values
- [x] Keys with spaces and quotes (injection prevention)
- [x] CLI mode (`append-object` command)
- [x] Error: no key=value pairs → exit 2
- [x] Error: invalid format (no `=`) → exit 2
- [x] Error: empty key → exit 2
- [x] Error: nonexistent file → exit 1
- [x] Error: non-array target path → exit 2
- [x] All existing tests pass (99 assertions, 12 files)

author: atzzcokek
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2042 

This PR resolves an issue where CSS `background` properties containing linear gradients with rgba() color values would return empty strings, while the same gradients using hex alpha notation worked correctly.

## Root Cause

1. **GRADIENT_REGEXP pattern issue**: The pattern used `[^)]+` which means "match anything except `)`". When parsing gradients with nested rgba() functions like `linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 1) 100%)`, the regex would stop at the first `)` that closes the rgba() function, failing to capture the entire gradient.

2. **String splitting issue**: The comma/space splitting logic didn't respect nested parentheses. When `getBackgroundImage()` split the gradient value by commas, it would incorrectly split inside rgba() functions, producing invalid fragments that couldn't be parsed.

## Solution

### 1. Updated GRADIENT_REGEXP
Changed the pattern to handle one level of nested parentheses:
```typescript
/^((repeating-linear|linear|radial|repeating-radial|conic|repeating-conic)-gradient)\(((?:[^()]|\([^()]*\))*)\)$/
```

### 2. Improved getGradient() method
Added logic to split commas while respecting parentheses depth.

### 3. Added helper functions
- `splitByComma()` - Splits on commas outside parentheses
- `splitBySpace()` - Splits on spaces/tabs outside parentheses

Both functions track parenthesis depth and only split when depth is 0.

### 4. Updated CSS parsers
- `getBackground()` uses `splitBySpace()`
- `getBackgroundImage()` uses `splitByComma()`

## Test Coverage

Added **15 comprehensive test cases**:
- rgba(), rgb(), hsla(), hsl() color functions
- All gradient types: linear, radial, conic, and their repeating variants
- Edge cases: multiple gradients, many color stops, decimal values, excessive whitespace
- Error cases: unbalanced parentheses, invalid gradient types
- Integration tests: background and backgroundImage properties

**All 7,184 tests pass** ✅

## Examples

### Before (broken)
```javascript
div.style.background = 'linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 1) 100%)';
console.log(div.style.background); // "" (empty string)
```

### After (fixed)
```javascript
div.style.background = 'linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 1) 100%)';
console.log(div.style.background); 
// "linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 1) 100%)" ✅
```

## Files Changed

- `CSSStyleDeclarationValueParser.ts` - Updated regex and getGradient() method
- `CSSStyleDeclarationPropertySetParser.ts` - Added helper functions, updated getBackground() and getBackgroundImage()
- `CSSStyleDeclarationValueParser.test.ts` - Added 11 unit tests
- `CSSStyleDeclaration.test.ts` - Added 4 integration tests

body:
### Motivation
- Cambiar la generación de respuestas a un LLM remoto que no requiera instalar modelos localmente, usando la API de Hugging Face Inference. 
- Mantener el flujo RAG: ingesta `.docx` → indexación TF‑IDF → retrieval → respuesta generada únicamente a partir del contexto recuperado con trazabilidad.

### Description
- Reemplaza la integración previa con Mistral por llamadas a `https://api-inference.huggingface.co/models/{model}` desde `src/rag_deque/answering.py` usando `urllib`, con manejo de errores HTTP/URL y parsing de `generated_text`.
- Añade soporte de autenticación vía `HF_API_KEY` o `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` y argumento CLI `--hf-api-key`, y cambia los flags CLI a `--hf-model`/`--hf-api-key` en `src/rag_deque/cli.py` (por defecto `google/flan-t5-large`).
- Conserva y adapta la construcción de contexto, umbral de baja confianza (`LOW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`) y trazabilidad de fuentes (archivo, sección, score, snippet) en la respuesta generada.
- Actualiza o añade implementación de ingesta, modelos e index/retrieval (`src/rag_deque/ingestion.py`, `src/rag_deque/models.py`, `src/rag_deque/retrieval.py`) y documentación en `README.md`; `requirements.txt` se deja vacío al usar la stdlib para HTTP.

### Testing
- `python -m compileall src` ejecutado con éxito. 
- `PYTHONPATH=src python -m rag_deque.ingestion --help` y `PYTHONPATH=src python -m rag_deque.cli --help` mostraron las ayudas correctamente. 
- Indexación end‑to‑end con un `.docx` sintético (`PYTHONPATH=src python -m rag_deque.ingestion --input-dir tmp_docs --output-dir data/index`) completada correctamente y generó el índice.

author: thememebanker
body:
<!-- Clearly explain the need for these changes: -->

AI agents need the ability to pay for premium API access automatically. When an agent encounters an HTTP 402 Payment Required response, it should be able to make a payment and continue. This PR adds blocks for the x402 HTTP payment protocol via Nory, enabling agents to make micropayments on Solana and 7 EVM chains with sub-400ms settlement.

### Changes 🏗️

- Added 5 new payment blocks in `backend/blocks/nory_x402.py`:
  - `NoryGetPaymentRequirementsBlock` - Get payment requirements for a resource (amount, networks, wallet address)
  - `NoryVerifyPaymentBlock` - Verify a signed payment transaction before settlement
  - `NorySettlePaymentBlock` - Submit a verified payment to the blockchain (~400ms)
  - `NoryTransactionLookupBlock` - Check the status of a previously submitted payment
  - `NoryHealthCheckBlock` - Check Nory service health and supported networks
- All blocks are in the `DATA` category
- Supports optional `NORY_API_KEY` credential (not required for public endpoints)
- Supports Solana (mainnet/devnet) and 7 EVM chains (Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Sei, IoTeX)

author: chet
body:
## Description

This is going to be a bit of a lift, but I think we can do it in a few different phases/layers, with the RPC layer being last. DNS and DHCP should be a good time.

In this first PR, on a more foundational front, in which we switch several types from `Ipv4Addr` to `IpAddr` across `api-model`, `api-db`, and `resource_pool`. It's not all of them, but taking baby steps.

For the database, since the Postgres `inet` and `cidr` types already support IPv6, we're taken care of there, and everything else flows naturally, including in resource pools. All existing data remains IPv4 and continues to work just the same as it did. Tests were added to verify `network_config` in the database still works:
- `test_managed_host_network_config_ipv4_json_roundtrip`: Make sure IPv4-backed configs [still] serialize/deserialize correctly.
- `test_managed_host_network_config_ipv4_json_format_unchanged`: Make sure JSON output for IPv4 is identical to `Ipv4Addr`.
- `test_managed_host_network_config_deserialize_legacy_ipv4_json`: Make sure IPv4 JSON strings (as stored in Postgres) parse into `IpAddr` correctly.
- `test_managed_host_network_config_ipv6_json_roundtrip`: Make sure IPv6 addresses *also* roundtrip correctly through JSON.
- `test_managed_host_network_config_deserialize_ipv6_json`: Make sure IPv6 JSON strings parses correctly also.
- `test_managed_host_network_config_default`: aaand make sure the `Default` config is unchanged.

For resource pools, they store values as strings in the DB and parse them via `from_str`. A couple of new tests were introduced to ensure the `allocate()` and `release()` functions still work the same with IPv4, and now support IPv6. Tests are:
- `test_ip_addr_parse_from_pool_strings`: Make sure v4 and v6 work.
- `test_ip_addr_to_string_format`: Make sure v4 and v6 work.

Made sure that no callers were doing any IPv4 specific operations like working with `.octets()` or anything; they generally all just store the result as an `Option` (which `Option<IpAddr>` is compatible), or call `.to_string()`, which tests were added for to verify.

Regarding some IPv6 matching we had to return an error, there were two `match` in `vpc_dpu_loopback.rs` that returned errors on `IpAddr::V6`, and have been removed, now that the resource pool is typed as `IpAddr`. Again, IPv4 and IPv6 now both work in this case.

author: copilot
body:
The notification preference logic was determining recipient identity by comparing email strings (`email == user.email`), which is brittle and conflates recipient type with address matching.

## Changes

- **Added `RecipientType` enum** (`User`, `Specialist`) to explicitly identify notification recipients
- **Updated notification tuple structure** from `(email, subject, body, notificationType)` to `(recipientType, email, subject, body, notificationType)` 
- **Replaced email comparison with pattern matching** on recipient type when determining whether to check notification preferences

## Example

Before:
```scala
val notificationsToSend: List[(String, String, String, NotificationType)] = ...
val emailsToSend: List[IO[Unit]] = notificationsToSend.flatMap {
  case (email, subject, body, notificationType) =>
    if email == user.email then
      // check preferences
    else
      // always send
}
```

After:
```scala
val notificationsToSend: List[(RecipientType, String, String, String, NotificationType)] = ...
val emailsToSend: List[IO[Unit]] = notificationsToSend.flatMap {
  case (recipientType, email, subject, body, notificationType) =>
    recipientType match
      case RecipientType.User => // check preferences
      case RecipientType.Specialist => // always send
}
```

This eliminates potential edge cases (matching emails, future CC/BCC support) and makes recipient handling explicit and type-safe.

author: syliow
body:
💡 **What:**
Replaced the Base64 file upload mechanism with `FormData` (multipart/form-data) in `app/page.tsx` and updated the backend API `app/api/generate/route.ts` to consume it.

🎯 **Why:**
The previous implementation read the entire file into memory as a Base64 string on the client (blocking the UI) and sent it as a JSON field. This increased the payload size by ~33% and caused memory spikes on the server during JSON parsing.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
- **Payload Size:** Reduced by ~33% (Binary vs Base64).
- **Latency:** End-to-end latency for small files remains low (~60ms). For larger files (10MB), this change avoids the overhead of Base64 encoding/decoding and JSON parsing, significantly reducing memory pressure on the server.
- **Client UX:** Removed `FileReader.readAsDataURL` which blocks the main thread for large files.

**Changes:**
- `app/page.tsx`: Updated `handleFileUpload` to store the raw `File` object and `callApi` to send `FormData` when a file is present.
- `app/api/generate/route.ts`: Updated to handle `multipart/form-data`, extract the file stream, and process it efficiently.
- `lib/types.ts` & `lib/validation.ts`: Updated `FileData` type and validation logic to support optional `data` (Base64) if `file` (File object) is provided.

- Move the app to a cleaner centered top-bar layout, rebrand to `Modo Gusto`, and make the app immediately browsable by loading community recipes by default.

- Improve calendar views and dashboard UX (upcoming meals for today/tomorrow and quick navigation) for better planning on mobile and desktop.

- UI / branding: renamed to `Modo Gusto`, added a new app icon and updated `frontend/public/index.html`, `frontend/public/manifest.json`, and `frontend/public/images/app-icon.svg` and refactored navigation into a fixed top-bar with inline links + hamburger off-canvas side menu.

# Before
import pyperclip

try:

except ImportError:
    pyperclip = None

CLIPBOARD_AVAILABLE = False
if pyperclip is not None:
    try:
        pyperclip.paste()
        CLIPBOARD_AVAILABLE = True
    except Exception:

```

author: alexhooketh
body:
Circle seems to have increased CCTP V2 fast-transfer fees on several destination chains (e.g. 1.3–1.5 bps on common EVMs).

This PR changes `CCTPV2Bridger` to compute `maxFee` from a chain-specific ppm table (ceil’d), instead of hardcoding 1 bps.

Table (ppm = 1e-6, 1 bps = 100 ppm):
- Ethereum (1): 100 ppm
- Arbitrum (42161): 130 ppm
- Base (8453): 130 ppm
- OP (10): 130 ppm
- World Chain (480): 130 ppm
- Unichain (130): 150 ppm

- Circle appears to accept fees >= required (but not below), so this should avoid underpay failures.
- No behavior change for USDT routes; this only affects the USDC CCTP V2 bridger.

Fixes the issue where Portal Home and Lock Terminal buttons were not visible on iPhone 16 Pro and other iOS devices in the admin sidebar. ## Problem On iOS Safari, the sidebar footer buttons were cut off and not visible due to how Safari handles viewport height with its dynamic UI chrome (address bar, toolbar). The sidebar used `h-screen` (100vh) which doesn't account for Safari's dynamic browser chrome, causing the footer section to be pushed below the visible viewport. ## Solution Changed the sidebar height utility class from `h-screen` to `h-dvh` (dynamic viewport height) in `sidebar.component.ts` line 32. The `h-dvh` utility properly adjusts to the actual available viewport height in iOS Safari, accounting for the browser's dynamic chrome elements. ## Changes Made - **File**: `src/app/ui/components/admin/sidebar/sidebar.component.ts` - **Change**: `h-screen` → `h-dvh` (line 32) The sidebar footer (lines 98-143) contains: - Portal Home link → navigates to `/dashboard` - Lock Terminal button → locks terminal via `authService.setStaffActive(false)` and redirects to `/staff-select` Layout uses flexbox with proper constraints: - Navigation: `flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0` (scrollable) - Footer: `flex-shrink-0` (fixed at bottom) ## Testing **Desktop (1024x768)** **Mobile (375x667)** **iPhone 16 Pro (390x844) - Fixed** Both Portal Home and Lock Terminal buttons are now visible and accessible at the bottom of the sidebar across all devices, including iOS. ## Verification - ✅ Code review completed - no issues found - ✅ Security scan completed - no vulnerabilities detected - ✅ Tested on iPhone 16 Pro viewport (390x844) - ✅ Both buttons visible and functional on all tested viewports

body:
## Describe your changes

  Summary

  - Fix refreshRulesMap() to rebuild the rules map from scratch instead of merging, so stale entries (Handle == 0) from failed flushes are naturally dropped
  - Add Handle == 0 guards to all delete paths (DeleteRouteRule, removeNatRule, removeLegacyRouteRule, DeleteDNATRule, RemoveInboundDNAT) that clean up stale entries instead of returning errors
  - Implement rollbackRules() for AddNatRule flush failures to clean up unflushed entries and decrement set counters
  - Change RemoveNatRule from fail-fast to error accumulation for cleanup resilience

  Problem

  When conn.Flush() fails in AddNatRule, rules are stored in the map with Handle == 0 (the kernel never assigned handles). The old refreshRulesMap() merged kernel rules into the existing map, so these stale entries persisted
  indefinitely. Any subsequent delete operation would fail on Handle == 0, which blocked further operations like re-adding the same NAT rule.

### Motivation
- Bug reports need a complete view of timing information across flows so diagnostics include every timer run (API calls, agenda steps, notes append steps). 
- Existing report scoping was filtering API logs but did not surface notes-append timings or a consolidated timer summary.

### Description
- Added a `Notes Append Trace` section to `generateBugReport` that includes `Notes_Append_Trace` entries when `reportType` is `meeting_notes` or `all` and prints step details and `duration_ms` values. 
- Introduced helpers `getApiNameFilters`, `getApiFlowFilters`, `filterApiRequestsByReportType`, and `filterApiResponsesByReportType` and updated usages in `generateBugReport` and `generateIssuesSummary` to centralize report-type scoping and prefer `request_id` linkage for response filtering. 
- Added `buildTimerEntries(apiResponses, agendaTraces, notesAppendTraces)` to aggregate API response, agenda trace, and notes-append trace durations into a consolidated `Timers` list that is sorted by timestamp and rendered in the report. 
- Replaced prior inline API-name filtering with calls to `filterApiRequestsByReportType` and `filterApiResponsesByReportType` to reduce cross-report noise and align response scoping with request linkage.

### Testing

author: amywieliczka
body:
This will cause no changes for static finding aids already stored in s3 (the oac-4 style static finding aids). Static finding aids previously below the component limit (always dynamically generated) will still be dynamically generated against the solr followers, but now they will also be stored in s3 and this content will be served the next time a request is issued. 

There is some risk, though: static finding aids above the previously configured component limit and without an oac-4 style static finding aid manually stored in s3 will now get static finding aids the next time someone tries to click that link. I'm not sure which arks fall into this category, though. Perhaps few enough, and perhaps the performance upgrade from the application-side tree traversal to the solr-side with the child doc transformer is enough to manage. 

On prd, as of noon Thursday February 12th, there are 73,360 finding aids with fewer than 300 components, 5,453 finding aids with more than 300 components, and 9,777 oac4-style static finding aids in s3. 

This PR should be understood as the first step towards migrating off these oac4-style static finding aids. Next steps are some architectural tests on oac-stage: 
- ensure solr's ALB timeout values are high enough (6 seconds, ideally)
- possibly increase arclight's ALB timeout as well
- check arclight for performance issues with deeply nested finding aids, large finding aids

Simultaneously, evaluate adding cinco ctrl's FindingAid model's last updated date field to the solr index, and using this field as part of the cache key _instead of_ timestamp and version. This would allow us to add the rake task to the airflow indexing job without needlessly re-running it every time textract finishes a pdf text extraction job. 

Alternatively, we could run the rake task as a cron job weekly? nightly? for some subset of supersized static finding aids. 

Simultaneously, also evaluate any changes we want to make to the oac5 style static finding aid display. Now is the time to make those changes.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for Unicode escape sequences in the JavaScript lexer, allowing developers to use `\uXXXX` (4-digit) and `\u{XXXXX}` (extended) escape sequences in identifiers, strings, and template literals.

## Key Changes
- **New `parse_unicode_escape()` function**: Parses both standard (`\uXXXX`) and extended (`\u{XXXXX}`) Unicode escape formats with proper validation
- **New `write_code_point()` function**: Converts Unicode code points to characters, handling surrogate pairs for code points above U+FFFF
- **Identifier parsing enhancement**: Modified identifier tokenization to recognize and decode Unicode escapes at the start and middle of identifiers
- **String literal support**: Added Unicode escape handling in both regular strings and template literals
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 12 new tests covering various Unicode escape scenarios (identifiers, strings, template literals, keyword resolution)

## Implementation Details
- Unicode escapes in identifiers are properly decoded before keyword resolution, so `\u0076\u0061\u0072` correctly resolves to the `var` keyword
- Extended Unicode format (`\u{...}`) supports 1-6 hex digits and validates code points don't exceed U+10FFFF
- Standard format (`\uXXXX`) requires exactly 4 hex digits
- Surrogate pair encoding is used for code points above U+FFFF to maintain JavaScript compatibility
- All escape sequences are properly tracked for line/column position updates

author: pierre-pretorius
body:
## Problem

`Bootstrap.stream_entries/3` sends an anonymous function via `:rpc.call` to copy cached entries from existing nodes when a new node joins the cluster. During rolling deploys, the new node has recompiled BEAM modules. Anonymous functions are bound to the sending node's module version and fail on nodes running different code, producing `{:badrpc, {:EXIT, {:badarg, ...}}}` which is silently swallowed.

This causes a cascade failure:

1. New node tries to bootstrap from old node — lambda RPC fails silently
2. New node starts with empty cache
3. Remaining old nodes restart, bootstrap from the already-empty new node
4. All cache data is lost

## Fix

Replace the anonymous function with an MFA call to a new public `do_stream_entries/1` function. MFA calls resolve on the remote node using its own code, so they work across code versions.

## Reproduction

A standalone test project demonstrating the bug is available at:
https://github.com/pierre-pretorius/nebulex_replication_test

---

That should be everything you need. Just make sure the base branch is set to `v2` before submitting.

Completely redesigns the diagnostics dashboard with a modern, data-driven interface featuring interactive Recharts visualizations, track-by-track filtering, and enhanced metric displays. Replaces static card layouts with dynamic bar charts showing prediction accuracy, tier performance, and exotic bet hit rates. Adds sortable track comparison table and introduces a sticky filter bar for easy track selection.

### Key Changes

**UI/UX Improvements:**
- New sticky track filter bar with chip-style buttons for quick filtering
- Replaced static tier table with animated bar chart showing win/ITM rates
- Added prediction accuracy chart comparing win/place/show rates vs. random chance
- New exotic bet hit rate chart (horizontal bar chart) for exacta/trifecta/superfecta combinations
- Sortable track comparison table with visual indicators for best/worst performing tracks
- Enhanced metric cards with larger typography and left border accent
- Smooth animations and transitions between filtered views using Framer Motion

**Data Visualization:**
- Integrated Recharts library for professional chart rendering
- Custom tooltip component with detailed breakdowns
- Reference lines showing random chance baseline
- Color-coded bars with gradient interpolation for exotic bets
- Dark theme compatibility with CSS variable overrides for Recharts SVG elements

**Functionality:**
- Track filtering system that recalculates all metrics in real-time
- Sortable columns in track comparison table (click to sort ascending/descending)
- Grade system (A-F) for prediction accuracy assessment
- Multiplier calculation showing how much better than random chance
- Calibration indicator for tier performance validation

**Code Quality:**
- Added helper functions: `getGrade()`, `lerpColor()` for color interpolation
- New component types: `FilteredMetrics`, `SortKey`, `SortDir`
- Memoized calculations for performance (filtered metrics, sorted tracks, best/worst tracks)
- Custom Recharts tooltip component for consistent styling
- Proper TypeScript typing throughout

**CSS Enhancements:**
- New `.diag-filter-bar` and `.diag-filter-chip` styles with hover states
- `.diag-chart-card` wrapper for consistent chart styling
- `.diag-comparison-table` with sortable header styling
- Recharts grid and legend overrides for dark theme
- Improved metric card styling with larger values and better hierarchy
- Removed legacy track card grid layout

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes)

- [ ] All existing tests pass (`npm run test`)
- [ ] New tests added for new functionality

- [ ] ESLint passes with no errors (`npm run lint`)
- [ ] Build succeeds (`npm run build`)

## Manual Testing

- [ ] Tested track filtering on mobile viewport (375px)
- [ ] Tested track filtering on desktop viewport
- [ ] Verified chart rendering with various data ranges
- [ ] Tested sorting functionality in track comparison table
- [ ] Verified tooltip interactions on hover/touch
- [ ] Tested with no data state
- [ ] Verified dark theme compatibility with Recharts

## Additional Notes

- Recharts library added as dependency for chart rendering
- Color constants defined at top of component for Recharts (CSS variables don't work in SVG)
- Track filtering preserves all other UI state (scroll position, etc.)
- Charts use `ResponsiveContainer` for mobile responsiveness

author: maherfsf
body:
## Description This PR establishes a robust, auditable, and immutable release and versioning strategy. It formalizes the "Manus" build as the canonical latest version and introduces mechanisms to prevent accidental modification of past releases. Key changes include: - **Canonical Release Folder**: `docs/releases/` now holds `latest.json` (machine-readable manifest) and `latest.md` (human-readable summary), along with versioned immutable snapshots (e.g., `docs/releases/v0.2.3/`). - **Archiving**: Historical documentation (`STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `PROOFS/`) is indexed under `docs/archive/` for traceability without mutation. - **Release Policy**: `docs/RELEASE_POLICY.md` defines immutability for past releases and the process for integrating future Manus updates. - **Guardrail Script**: `scripts/release-guard.mjs` prevents modifications to existing immutable release folders. - **Manus Update Checker**: `scripts/check-manus-updates.mjs` helps identify new Manus contributions for potential adoption. - **Release Snapshot Creator**: `scripts/create-release-snapshot.mjs` automates the creation of new immutable release folders. - **AWS Deployment Alignment**: Updated deployment guides to include mandatory steps for publishing the release manifest to S3 and archiving release bundles. - **README Update**: Reflects the new release and versioning model, including updated badges with latest verified stats. The primary goal is to ensure clear, verifiable versioning, easy rollback, and a structured approach to integrating new development, preventing inconsistencies and accidental overwrites. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] 🔧 Configuration/Infrastructure change - [ ] ♻️ Refactoring (no functional changes) ## Related Issues ## Checklist ### Required (must pass before merge) - [x] `pnpm test` passes (all 736+ tests) - *Verified by AI* - [x] `node scripts/release-gate.mjs` passes (10/10 gates) - *Verified by AI* - [x] No new TypeScript errors introduced (existing 141 errors are known) - *Verified by AI* - [x] No secrets or credentials committed ### Recommended - [x] Added/updated tests for new functionality - *New scripts added* - [x] Updated documentation if needed - *Extensive documentation updates* - [ ] Tested in browser: affected pages render correctly - *No UI changes* - [ ] Checked Arabic (RTL) layout if UI changes - *No UI changes* ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Testing Notes To test the new release management features: 1. **Release Guard**: - Run `pnpm release:guard`. It should pass. - Try to modify a file inside `docs/releases/v0.2.3/` (e.g., `docs/releases/v0.2.3/README.md`). - Run `pnpm release:guard` again. It should fail with an immutability violation. - Revert the change to `docs/releases/v0.2.3/README.md`. 2. **Manus Update Checker**: - Run `pnpm release:check-manus`. It will list Manus-authored commits since the latest tag (or indicate none). 3. **Release Snapshot Creator**: - Run `pnpm release:snapshot v0.2.4` (or any new version). - Verify that `docs/releases/v0.2.4/` is created with `manifest.json` and `README.md`. - Verify that `docs/releases/latest.json` is *not* automatically updated by this script (it's a manual step as per policy). ## Deployment Notes - **Publish Release Manifest**: After deployment, the `docs/releases/latest.json` file **must** be copied to the designated S3 bucket (e.g., `s3://yeto-assets/releases/latest.json`) to make the current version publicly verifiable. - **Archive Release Bundle**: The `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z/` folder for the deployed version should be synced to an S3 backup bucket (e.g., `s3://yeto-backups/releases/vX.Y.Z`) for rollback purposes. - **Production DNS**: Ensure `yeto.causewaygrp.com` is publicly resolvable to allow external verification of the deployed version. - **`package.json` Version**: Remember to update the `version` field in `package.json` to match the new release tag when cutting a new release, so runtime health endpoints reflect the correct version. ---

 

--- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Mostly documentation and simple Node scripts around `git diff/log` and file copying; no runtime application logic is changed. Main risk is CI friction if `release:guard` is adopted with an incorrect `RELEASE_GUARD_BASE` or unexpected release-folder edits. > > **Overview** > Adds an **audit-friendly release/versioning structure** under `docs/releases/`, including a canonical `latest.json`/`latest.md` manifest plus an immutable snapshot for `v0.2.3` with proof-pack links and verified counts. > > Introduces **release tooling and policy**: new `pnpm` scripts to (1) guard against modifications to existing `docs/releases/v*/` folders (`release:guard`), (2) snapshot the current `latest.json` into a new versioned release directory (`release:snapshot`), and (3) list Manus-authored commits since the latest tag (`release:check-manus`), alongside a new `docs/RELEASE_POLICY.md` and archive index. > > Updates ops/docs to **publish the release manifest to S3** for production verification (AWS + production runbooks) and refreshes README badges/counts and adds a "Release & Versioning" section; `STATUS.md` is explicitly marked as historical. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit c84a10defd1a3756a383796496135c574c5de7a7. body: ## Description This PR adds a new enrichment task (`create_chunk_associations`) that analyzes document chunks for semantic similarity using LLM-based comparison and creates weighted "associated_with" edges between them in the knowledge graph. Will close #1333 The task uses vector search for candidate selection to find semantically related chunks, then uses an LLM to verify and score the similarity. ## Acceptance Criteria * Configurable similarity threshold (default 0.7) * Configurable min chunk length and top-k candidates * Creates weighted edges with association type and reasoning metadata * Integrates as enrichment task in the memify pipeline ### How to verify Run the example script: ```bash python examples/python/chunk_associations_example.py ``` ### Example output ``` Adding text chunks to cognee: 1. River dolphins are freshwater mammals found in South America and Asia. 2. Scientists study dolphin behavior in Amazon rivers to understand their communication. 3. Python is a high-level programming language widely used for data science. 4. Dolphins use echolocation to navigate and hunt in murky river waters. 5. Machine learning models require large datasets for training. 6. The Amazon river dolphin, also known as boto, is pink in color. Text added successfully. Running cognify to create knowledge graph... Cognify process complete. Running memify to create chunk associations... Memify process complete. Querying for chunk associations... Found 6 chunk associations: 1. Similarity: 0.85 Type: topical Chunk 1: River dolphins are freshwater mammals found in South America and Asia. Chunk 2: Scientists study dolphin behavior in Amazon rivers to understand their communica Reasoning: Chunks are semantically related as they both discuss dolphins and their habitats, with chunk 2 providing more specific information on research related to river dolphins. 2. Similarity: 0.85 Type: topical Chunk 1: River dolphins are freshwater mammals found in South America and Asia. Chunk 2: The Amazon river dolphin, also known as boto, is pink in color. Reasoning: Chunks 1 and 2 are clearly related as they discuss the same species, Amazon river dolphins/boto. 3. Similarity: 0.85 Type: topical Chunk 1: River dolphins are freshwater mammals found in South America and Asia. Chunk 2: Dolphins use echolocation to navigate and hunt in murky river waters. Reasoning: Both chunks discuss river dolphins and their behavior in freshwater environments. 4. Similarity: 0.70 Type: topical Chunk 1: Python is a high-level programming language widely used for data science. Chunk 2: Machine learning models require large datasets for training. Reasoning: The chunks are related as they involve the broader topic of programming and data science. 5. Similarity: 0.85 Type: topical Chunk 1: Dolphins use echolocation to navigate and hunt in murky river waters. Chunk 2: Scientists study dolphin behavior in Amazon rivers to understand their communica Reasoning: Both chunks discuss dolphins, with Chunk 1 covering navigation/hunting and Chunk 2 highlighting scientific study. 6. Similarity: 0.80 Type: topical Chunk 1: The Amazon river dolphin, also known as boto, is pink in color. Chunk 2: Scientists study dolphin behavior in Amazon rivers to understand their communica Reasoning: Both mention Amazon river dolphins, with Chunk 1 describing color and Chunk 2 examining behavior. ``` ### Tests Run tests: ```bash pytest cognee/tests/test_chunk_associations.py -v ``` All 6 tests pass: - `test_chunk_associations_creates_edges_between_similar_chunks` - verifies edges are created - `test_chunk_associations_respects_similarity_threshold` - verifies threshold filtering - `test_chunk_associations_includes_metadata` - verifies edge properties - `test_chunk_associations_with_cypher_query` - verifies Cypher search works - `test_chunk_associations_handles_single_chunk` - verifies no edges with 1 chunk - `test_chunk_associations_configurable_parameters` - verifies min_chunk_length filtering ## Type of Change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Pre-submission Checklist - [x] **I have tested my changes thoroughly before submitting this PR** - [x] **This PR contains minimal changes necessary to address the issue/feature** - [x] My code follows the project's coding standards and style guidelines - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] All new and existing tests pass - [x] I have searched existing PRs to ensure this change hasn't been submitted already - [x] My commits have clear and descriptive messages ## DCO Affirmation I affirm that all code in every commit of this pull request conforms to the terms of the Topoteretes Developer Certificate of Origin. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added semantic chunk association: automatic detection and linking of related text chunks using vector + LLM assessments; outputs include boolean similarity, numeric score, association type, and short rationale. Configurable thresholds, min-length, candidate limits, and persistence to the knowledge graph. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive tests for association creation, weight normalization, threshold behavior, metadata presence, queryability, and no-edge cases. * **Chores** * Added an end-to-end example script demonstrating the chunk association workflow.

body:
We don't need to export the type metadata address point alias in clients that lazily emit other module's type metadata. There will be an exported metadata symbol in the originating module for that purpose.

Instead, satisfy any local uses of the metadata address point uses by its underlying address computation.

This is to workaround a bug where LLVM generates the wrong assembly for weak aliases that point to an offset of another symbol.

```
@"$e1C7MyClassCySiGN" = weak_odr hidden alias %swift.type, getelementptr
inbounds (<{ ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr }>,
ptr @"$e1C7MyClassCySiGMf", i32 0, i32 1)
```

Generates:

```
.weak_reference _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
.private_extern _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
.alt_entry  _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
  _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN = _$e1C7MyClassCySiGMf+8
```

Instead of

```
.weak_definition _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
.private_extern _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
.alt_entry  _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN
  _$e1C7MyClassCySiGN = _$e1C7MyClassCySiGMf+8
```

Leading for "weak"ness to be ignored and duplicate type medata symbol linkage errors.

### Motivation
- Make the first impression match the reference by showing an autoplaying, muted looping reel as the full-screen hero with no visible header or text on entry.  
- Reveal the site navigation only after the user scrolls so the reel remains the initial focus.  
- Consolidate content by moving the “Sobre mí” content into the homepage, add the repeating call-to-action line, and keep the projects tiles accessible below.  
- Improve static-host compatibility by normalizing resource paths and adding minimal front-matter to pages.

### Description
- Implemented a full-screen reel hero using a privacy-enhanced YouTube embed (`youtube-nocookie`) with autoplay/mute/loop parameters and CSS to set the hero to `100vh` (`index.html` changes).  
- Hid the header by default and added a scroll-triggered visibility toggle that adds/removes `.is-visible` on `.site-navbar` via a small inline script to reveal the menu after scrolling.  
- Moved the About section into the homepage as a centered intro block, inserted a marquee-style repeating line `DISEÑEMOS JUNTOS` with CSS animation, and (re)placed the `Proyectos` grid below the marquee; added `intro-text`, `about-section`, `marquee` and `projects-section` markup and styles in `index.html`.  
- Normalized asset and script references across many pages to use root-relative paths (example: `css/...` → `/css/...`, `images\foo.jpg` → `/images/foo.jpg`) and added Jekyll-style front-matter (`---`) headers to HTML pages to improve static hosting behavior.

### Testing
- Launched a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` and ran a Playwright script that opened `http://127.0.0.1:8000/index.html` and captured a full-page screenshot which completed successfully and produced the artifact `artifacts/home-scroll.png`.  
- Verified `#lightgallery` initialization remains intact by running the site and confirming the existing `$('#lightgallery').lightGallery();` initialization executes without errors during the page load.

author: aliazading
body:
Fixed the management panel issues where traffic consumption and online user counts were consistently zero. The root cause was twofold: (1) Dante was unable to write its usage logs due to strict systemd sandboxing on Ubuntu, and (2) the application's log parsing logic did not support the specific log format of the installed Dante version.

The fix involves:
- Implementing a systemd override for `danted.service` to grant write access to `/var/log/danted.log`.
- Adjusting log file permissions so the service user has write access.
- Updating the `app.py` parsing logic to correctly identify connection/disconnection events and extract byte counts from the new log format, while preserving support for older formats.

Released on 2026-02-03.

Check out the [blog post](https://astral.sh/blog/ruff-v0.15.0) for a migration
guide and overview of the changes!

##### Breaking changes

- Ruff now formats your code according to the 2026 style guide. See the formatter section below or in the blog post for a detailed list of changes.

- The linter now supports block suppression comments. For example, to suppress `N803` for all parameters in this function:

  ```python
  # ruff: disable[N803]
  def foo(
      legacyArg1,
      legacyArg2,
      legacyArg3,
      legacyArg4,
  ): ...
  # ruff: enable[N803]
  ```

  See the [documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/#block-level) for more details.

- The `ruff:alpine` Docker image is now based on Alpine 3.23 (up from 3.21).

- The `ruff:debian` and `ruff:debian-slim` Docker images are now based on Debian 13 "Trixie" instead of Debian 12 "Bookworm."

- Binaries for the `ppc64` (64-bit big-endian PowerPC) architecture are no longer included in our releases. It should still be possible to build Ruff manually for this platform, if needed.

- Ruff now resolves all `extend`ed configuration files before falling back on a default Python version.

##### Stabilization

- [`blocking-http-call-httpx-in-async-function`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blocking-http-call-httpx-in-async-function)

  (`FURB171`)

- [`unnecessary-lambda`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-lambda) (`PLW0108`)
- [`unnecessary-empty-iterable-within-deque-call`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-empty-iterable-within-deque-call)

The following behaviors have been stabilized:

- The `--output-format` flag is now respected when running Ruff in `--watch` mode, and the `full` output format is now used by default, matching the regular CLI output.
- [`builtin-attribute-shadowing`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/builtin-attribute-shadowing/) (`A003`) now detects the use of shadowed built-in names in additional contexts like decorators, default arguments, and other attribute definitions.
- [`duplicate-union-member`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/duplicate-union-member/) (`PYI016`) now considers `typing.Optional` when searching for duplicate union members.
- [`split-static-string`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/split-static-string/) (`SIM905`) now offers an autofix when the `maxsplit` argument is provided, even without a `sep` argument.
- [`dict-get-with-none-default`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/dict-get-with-none-default/) (`SIM910`) now applies to more types of key expressions.
- [`super-call-with-parameters`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/super-call-with-parameters/) (`UP008`) now has a safe fix when it will not delete comments.
- [`unnecessary-default-type-args`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-default-type-args/) (`UP043`) now applies to stub (`.pyi`) files on Python versions before 3.13.

##### Formatter

This release introduces the new 2026 style guide, with the following changes:

### Motivation
- Provide a repeatable, versioned schema migration path by introducing Liquibase instead of ad-hoc SQL executed at startup.
- Ensure the in-memory H2 database is initialized consistently and seeded with sample data for development and testing.

### Description
- Add Liquibase and H2 JDBC dependencies in `build.gradle.kts` by adding `org.liquibase:liquibase-core` and `com.h2database:h2`.

author: kristjanesperanto
body:
Fixes #447 - Restores required fields that were incorrectly made optional in #443.

### Problem

When `CalendarComponentCommon` was introduced in #443 to share fields across VEVENT, VTODO, and VJOURNAL, all shared fields became optional (using `?`). This broke TypeScript compilation for users who relied on fields like `uid`, `dtstamp`, and `start` being required, causing a lot of type errors.

I’m sorry for any inconvenience.

### Solution

Override optional fields from `CalendarComponentCommon` to make RFC 5545 required fields non-optional:

**VEvent:**
- `uid` - required (RFC 5545)
- `dtstamp` - required (RFC 5545)
- `start` - required (RFC 5545 for VEVENT)
- `datetype` - required (always present with start)
- `summary` - required (practically always present)

**VTodo & VJournal:**
- `uid` - required (RFC 5545)
- `dtstamp` - required (RFC 5545)

### Note

This intentionally does **NOT** restore all previously required fields. Fields like `method`, `location`, `description`, `organizer`, `transparency`, `class`, `url`, `completion`, `created`, `lastmodified` remain optional because they are optional per RFC 5545.

### Testing

To prevent regressions like Issue #447 where fields became unintentionally optional I added TypeScript type tests.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Stricter TypeScript typings for calendar items: required RFC‑5545 fields (e.g., uid, timestamps, start, summary) are now enforced.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive type-only TypeScript tests to validate required vs optional calendar fields at compile time.

* **Chores**
  * Integrated TypeScript type checking into the test pipeline and added build scripts for time zone data updates.

<!-- Replace XXXX with the issue number. Issue will be auto-linked -->
Jira issue: SWATCH-4429

## Description
Using DISTINCT is a "computationally expensive" DB operation that is
currently providing zero value in this query because the data is
already unique due to the join on the measurement table.

This affects only the query used during the tally process and
should not affect the Tally API.

This patch also adds a missing try-with-resources when streaming snapshots.

**Note:**
I believe that distinct was originally used here, because prior to Hibernate 6, hibernate would not de-duplicate the results while streaming results from a query that joins on a child enity.

Implements flippable badge cards, explicit SSO account confirmation, and end-to-end featured badge selection.

## Badge Display Infrastructure

**BadgeMedallion component** - Flippable card with 3D flip animation. Front shows medal icon + name with optional highlight state (gradient + sparkle). Back shows description + earned date.

```tsx
<BadgeMedallion 
  name="Master Trainer"
  description="Completed 100+ training sessions"
  earnedDate="2024-01-15"
  highlighted={true}
/>
```

**Badge metadata flow** - Simplified `HomeTab.badgeDefinitions` from `BadgeType[]` to `{ id: string; name: string }[]` for minimal coupling.

## Featured Badge Support

Complete data flow for user-selected featured badges:

```tsx
// User schema
interface User {
  featured_badge_id?: string
}

// HomeTab computes display name
const featuredBadge = user.featured_badge_id
  ? badgeDefinitions.find(b => b.id === user.featured_badge_id)?.name
  : undefined

// NameBadge ready to display
<NameBadge featuredBadgeName={featuredBadge} />
```

## SSO Account Confirmation

Changed authentication flow to require explicit confirmation when existing account detected:

```tsx
// Before: immediate authentication
onAuthenticated(userExists.user, userExists.tenant)

// After: confirmation step
setExistingAccount({ user, tenant })
setStep('account_confirm')
```

New `account_confirm` step displays user identity (name, email, role, tenant). Applied to all SSO handlers (standard, Google, Apple). Device access recording moved to confirmation handler with error handling.

## Supporting Changes

- Icon imports: Sparkle, ShieldCheck, UserFocus, UserCircle (DeveloperTab, ProfileTab)
- BadgeAward import added to seed-data.ts

Integrate Manus IM build system with automated CI/CD pipeline to EVA-PARADIS repository.

## Background
This integration is being transferred from the Eva_Paradis repository which will be archived. The EVA-PARADIS repo contains the actual Eva Paradis Content Engine application (Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript).

## Files to Add

### 1. `.github/workflows/manus-im-build.yml`
Create a GitHub Actions workflow for automated builds and deployments.

```yaml
name: Manus IM Build and Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - bizbuildersai
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - bizbuildersai
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          if [ -f package.json ]; then
            npm ci
          else
            echo "No package.json found, skipping dependency installation"
          fi
      
      - name: Run build
        run: npm run build --if-present
      
      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test --if-present
      
      - name: Upload build artifacts
        if: success()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-artifacts
          path: |
            dist/
            build/
            out/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  deploy-manus-im:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/bizbuildersai' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Download build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-artifacts
          path: ./artifacts
      
      - name: Deploy to Manus IM
        env:
          MANUS_IM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MANUS_IM_API_KEY }}
          MANUS_IM_ENDPOINT: ${{ secrets.MANUS_IM_ENDPOINT }}
        run: |
          echo "Deploying to Manus IM..."
          # Add your Manus IM deployment commands here
          # Example: curl -X POST $MANUS_IM_ENDPOINT/deploy -H "Authorization: Bearer $MANUS_IM_API_KEY" -F "build=@./artifacts"
          echo "Deployment configuration ready. Please configure MANUS_IM_API_KEY and MANUS_IM_ENDPOINT secrets in GitHub repository settings."
```

### 2. `manus-im.config.json`
Create Manus IM specific build configuration.

```json
{
  "name": "eva-paradis",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Content Hub and Revenue Engine - Manus IM Build Configuration",

    "framework": "node",

    "buildCommand": "npm run build",

  },

    "type": "static",
    "environment": "production",
    "autoPublish": true,
    "regions": ["us-east-1"]
  },
  "hooks": {
    "preBuild": [],
    "postBuild": [],
    "preDeploy": [],
    "postDeploy": []
  },

    "NODE_VERSION": "20",

  }
}
```

### 3. `.env.example`
Add Manus IM environment variables template.

```

# Build Settings
BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR=dist
BUILD_TARGET=production

# Deployment Settings
DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT=production
DEPLOY_REGION=us-east-1

# Manus IM Integration

body:
## Summary
This PR improves task and deliverable management by automatically syncing deliverable statuses when task statuses change, optimizes database queries with proper indexing, and enhances the dashboard hours display to show remaining hours instead of total hours.

## Key Changes

- **Auto-sync deliverables on task status changes**: When a task's status is updated (via both `update` and `updateStatus` mutations), linked deliverables are automatically updated to maintain consistency:
  - Task marked "done" → deliverable marked "complete"
  - Task marked "in_review" → deliverable marked "in_review"
  - Task marked "in_progress" → deliverable marked "in_progress" (if not started)
  - Task unmarked from "done" → deliverable reverted to "in_progress"

- **Add database index for deliverables**: Added `by_taskId` index to the deliverables table schema to optimize queries filtering by taskId

- **Optimize deliverable queries**: Updated `getByTask` query in `convex/deliverables.ts` to use the new index for better performance

- **Improve dashboard hours display**: 
  - Calculate remaining hours (excluding done and cancelled tasks)
  - Show remaining hours when no actual hours are logged
  - Display actual hours when time tracking has begun

## Implementation Details

The deliverable sync logic is implemented in both the `update` and `updateStatus` mutations to ensure consistency regardless of which mutation is called. The logic handles edge cases like preventing duplicate status updates and properly reverting deliverables when tasks are moved out of "done" status.

author: copilot
body:
Caching tests reset cache stats but not the cache itself, allowing pre-populated data to cause false positives and order-dependent failures.

## Changes

Applied to all indicator test files (`test_atr.py`, `test_bollinger_bands.py`, `test_ema.py`, `test_ichimoku_cloud.py`, `test_macd.py`, `test_rsi.py`):

- Clear cache data with `indicator_cache.cache_data.clear()` before each cache hit test
- Assert exact hit/miss counts instead of comparing deltas

**Before:**
```python
indicator_cache.reset_stats()
result_1 = calculate_indicator(data)
first_misses = indicator_cache.misses
result_2 = calculate_indicator(data)
assert indicator_cache.misses == first_misses  # May already be cached
```

**After:**
```python
indicator_cache.cache_data.clear()
indicator_cache.reset_stats()
result_1 = calculate_indicator(data)
assert indicator_cache.misses == 1
result_2 = calculate_indicator(data)
assert indicator_cache.misses == 1 and indicator_cache.hits == 1
```

author: ivan-chong
body:
This plugin allows the user to select an input-related slice and understand the lifecycle of that event from the initial touch event to the frame.

There are two main features which this plugin provides:

1) Visualisation of the input lifecycle as "flows" on the UI. This
   allows the user the ability to trace the lifecycle visually and
easily correlate the events which contributed to a Frame, and vice versa.

2) It also presents the latency information as a table which allows the
   user to inspect the total latency of the event lifecycle, as well as
its constituent stages. This allows the user to quickly diagnose which stage is causing issues.

This is accompanied by a tab which allows toggling of the flows per channel (the visualisation defaults to showing a single lifecycle channel at a time for performance and visual clutter reasons). It also allows easy pinning of tracks for a given lifecycle and input channel. The latency table is also shown, with links which allow the user to select particular input events of interest.

author: geoaziz
body:
### Motivation
- Fix confusing navigation on auth pages so authenticated visitors hitting `/login` or `/signup` are immediately redirected to role-appropriate pages (`ADMIN` → `/admin`, `SELLER` → `/dashboard`, otherwise `/`).
- Make role information available to client-side pages to avoid incorrect fallback redirects and to help debug session verification failures.

### Description
- Return the user's `role` from the session verification endpoint by loading the user doc from `adminDb` in `src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts` so clients can make role-aware decisions.
- Update middleware (`src/middleware.ts`) to read the session cookie from `request.cookies`, log verification failures, clear invalid cookies, and continue redirecting by role for auth pages and protected routes.
- Add client-side session checks in `src/app/login/page.tsx` and `src/app/signup/page.tsx` using a `useEffect` that calls `GET /api/auth/session` and `router.replace(...)` to immediately reroute authenticated users by role.
- Add warning logs around session verification to aid troubleshooting and reduce silent failures.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

author: mhsnook
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces team-level metadata support to Scenetest, allowing teams to be defined with optional name, ownership paths, and tags. A new `defineTeam()` helper provides type-safe team definitions, while maintaining backward compatibility with plain `TeamConfig` exports.

## Key Changes

- **New Types**: Added `TeamMeta`, `TeamDef`, and `ResolvedTeam` types to support metadata-enriched team definitions
  - `TeamMeta`: Contains optional `name`, `owns` (URL paths), and `tags` (key-value pairs)
  - `TeamDef`: Full team definition with `actors` and optional metadata
  - `ResolvedTeam`: Internal representation splitting actors and metadata

- **New `defineTeam()` Helper**: Exported from `config.ts` and `index.ts` for type-safe team definitions with metadata

- **Team Discovery**: Updated `discoverTeams()` to normalize both plain `TeamConfig` and `TeamDef` exports into `ResolvedTeam` format via new `resolveTeam()` function

- **TeamManager Updates**: 
  - Now works with `ResolvedTeam[]` instead of `TeamConfig[]`
  - Added `getTeamMeta()` method to retrieve metadata for a team index
  - `TeamSession` now stores and exposes team metadata via `meta` property

- **Context Propagation**: 
  - `SceneContext` and `FlowContext` now include `team: TeamMeta` field
  - Team metadata passed to flow functions for `[team.field]` interpolation in DSL text

- **Interpolation Support**: Team metadata (tags, name, owns) now available for string interpolation in markdown scenes and reactive flows

- **HTML Report**: Updated report generation to display team name when available, falling back to team index

- **Test Updates**: Added `team: {}` to test scene reports to match new schema

## Implementation Details

- Backward compatible: Plain `Record<string, ActorConfig>` exports still work
- Team metadata is optional; teams without metadata get an empty `meta: {}` object
- `owns` can be a string or array; converted to comma-separated string for interpolation
- Tags are flattened into interpolation context alongside name and owns

## Summary
- **New tool: `scan_terminal_security`** — Auto-discovers and scans dotfiles, CI configs, env files, shell scripts for Unicode homograph attacks, ANSI escape injections, and suspicious URL patterns. Inspired by [terminal-security-scanner](https://github.com/HomenShum/terminal-security-scanner).
- **Daily tool generation pipeline** (`scripts/tool-gen/`) — 4 scripts + GitHub Actions workflow that reads daily brief signals, identifies tool gaps via Claude Haiku, generates McpTool code via Claude Sonnet, patches files deterministically, validates with tsc + vitest, and creates a PR automatically

  ├─ tsc --noEmit + vitest → validation gate
